justification: Two lines of test dependencies plus documentation. No product code, no served output, no database. Not Minor, because it changes WHAT CI RUNS: 45 tests that never executed in CI now do, and the dependency-skip ratchet floor drops to zero, so a future regression in any of those 45 becomes a red build instead of nothing. A change that alters the gate's coverage deserves the tier the gate itself is held to.

falsifiable_check.command: python -m pytest tests/ -q  AND  python scripts/check_dependency_skips.py
falsifiable_check.fails_when: The suite goes from 3925 passed / 20 skipped to 3970 passed / 2 skipped, and the ratchet reports 0 against a baseline of 0. It goes red three ways. (1) If either library fails to install in CI, the 40 shapely-dependent and 5 matplotlib-dependent tests revert to skipping or vanishing from collection, the census counts them, and check_dependency_skips.py fails because the baseline now says zero and it enforces EXACTLY in both directions. (2) If any of the 45 recovered tests actually fails, pytest is red -- and CI no longer runs with -x, so it reports all of them rather than stopping at the first. (3) If a NEW dependency-driven skip appears anywhere, the ratchet fails on the unknown key. The absence of the libraries was proven to be the cause, not assumed: injecting a PYTHONPATH stub whose shapely.py and matplotlib.py raise ImportError reproduces the old numbers exactly (3925/20, 3944 selected), and removing the stub reproduces the new ones (3970/2, 3972 selected). That 28-test difference in SELECTED count is the finding described in residual_risk.
falsifiable_check.external_authority: pip's resolution of shapely==2.1.2 and matplotlib==3.11.0 from PyPI decides whether the libraries are present; the pytest collector decides how many tests exist. Neither is produced by this repo, and the before/after was measured by simulating absence rather than by re-reading the baseline this change wrote.

pre_impl.existing_data: dependency-skip-baseline.json, written by #879, is the authoritative record of what CI actually skips: shapely 13, numpy+matplotlib+PIL 5, total 20, classified 18. It also already named the fix -- 'shapely ships manylinux wheels; most likely genuinely installable, so these 13 are the cheapest to win back' -- and identified matplotlib as the only missing member of its group, with numpy and pillow already in CI's transitive closure. #879's PyMuPDF entry in requirements-test.txt is the pattern followed here: pin to the version requirements.txt already carries, and say in a comment which tests were dark and why.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: PR #890 reported SIX packages that tests import but CI never installs. Only TWO are real. pandas, pillow and requests are present in CI's transitive closure (pvlib pulls pandas; the baseline states numpy and pillow are already there) and cause no skip; whitebox is deliberately replaced with a MagicMock at tests/conftest_mocks.py:120-124 when absent, so nothing skips on it either. scripts/doc_claims.py reasons about DECLARED packages and cannot see a transitive install closure, so it over-reports. That is a 4-in-6 false-positive rate on the dependency check specifically, materially worse than the ~2.4 percent floor PR #890 quoted for the path check, and the two must not be quoted as one number. The tool still earned its keep: shapely and matplotlib are genuine, and finding them is what exposed the 28 uncollected tests.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: No new machinery. Two pins added to the file CI installs, and the existing ratchet's baseline lowered to match -- the ratchet was built for exactly this and enforces both directions, so lowering it is what locks the recovery in. The tracker entries are logged, not fixed: DQ-54 (git-hook variables) and DQ-55 (documented-but-absent workflows) are recorded as open with their evidence, because a swept finding that lives only in a chat message is the doc-decay failure this campaign exists to stop.

functions: N/A — no functions are added or modified. The change is two dependency pins, one baseline file, and documentation.
values: N/A — no database or API values are read.

break_it.scenario: shapely or matplotlib fails to build on CI's runner image, so the install step succeeds partially or the import still fails at test time.
break_it.what_happens: The affected tests revert to skipping, the census counts them, and check_dependency_skips.py fails the build because the baseline is now zero and it enforces exactly in both directions. The build goes red rather than quietly returning to the old state.
break_it.how: Both are pinned to the versions requirements.txt already carries and both ship manylinux wheels for CI's Python 3.12, so no system libraries are needed; the ratchet catches it regardless of the reason.
break_it.repro: pip uninstall -y shapely matplotlib && python -m pytest tests/ -q && python scripts/check_dependency_skips.py

break_it.scenario: A future change breaks one of the 45 newly-running tests, and someone silences it with a module-level pytest.importorskip rather than fixing it.
break_it.what_happens: The whole file leaves COLLECTION rather than registering a skip, so the census reads zero and the ratchet stays green while the tests cease to exist. This is not hypothetical -- it is exactly how tests/test_sydney_water_gsp_ingest.py hid 28 tests until now.
break_it.how: Recorded in the baseline under _ratchet_blind_spot with the mechanism and the number that would catch it (the collected-test total, not the skip count). Deliberately not fixed here: adding a collected-count ratchet is its own change with its own false-positive profile, and bundling it into a dependency PR is how a gate arrives unreviewed.
break_it.repro: python -m pytest tests/ -q --collect-only -o addopts= | tail -1   # 3991 collected; a module-level importorskip drops it silently

break_it.scenario: The Sydney Water ingest tests, dark since they were written, turn out to have been failing all along -- they cover the price parse, the status derivation that drives user-facing serviceability wording, and the geometry coercion.
break_it.what_happens: They pass. All 28 collected and 28 passed, and the full suite is 3970 passed / 2 skipped with zero failures. A failure here would have been a FINDING about served serviceability wording, not a regression to paper over, so it was checked before the baseline was lowered rather than after.
break_it.how: Measured with the libraries installed locally at the same pinned versions before any file was edited; the absence was reproduced with a PYTHONPATH stub to confirm the libraries were the only variable.

break_it.scenario: Someone reads the new baseline of zero as 'no tests are dark' and stops looking.
break_it.what_happens: Zero means no test SKIPPED for a missing import. It does not mean every test runs: a module-level importorskip, a conftest collect_ignore entry, and a test that never got written all read as zero. The two remaining skips are deliberate env-gated live Gemini smoke tests.
break_it.how: The _ratchet_blind_spot key in dependency-skip-baseline.json states the limit in the file a reader has open when they form the belief, rather than in a PR body they will never see again.

mutation_analysis: The change is two dependency pins, so classical mutation testing does not apply -- there is no branch to invert. The equivalent was done by simulating the mutation that matters: making the libraries absent via a PYTHONPATH stub that raises ImportError. That reproduces the pre-change numbers exactly (3925 passed, 20 skipped, 3944 selected) and turns the ratchet red against the new baseline, which is the only way this change can regress. The three tracker entries were verified rather than asserted: DQ-53b by re-running #883's five cases through the hardened helper at both current main and commit a7edd825; DQ-54 by probing hook environments in throwaway repos (plain and worktree) and then demonstrating a wrong-repository answer live; DQ-55 by reading each citing document to separate a migration table from a live-infrastructure table, which reduced the count from the 13 filenames the tool flagged to the 3 documents that actually make a false current-state claim. Sol found the one arithmetic error in this report and it is corrected rather than rounded: the census's 'shapely: 13' is 12 TESTS (all in tests/test_solar_yield.py) plus ONE entry whose id is a FILE, tests/test_sydney_water_gsp_ingest.py, because a module-level importorskip records the module and collects nothing. So the recovery reconciles exactly as 12 + 5 + 28 = 45, matching the 3925 -> 3970 delta; the earlier reading of 13 + 5 + 28 = 46 double-counted that file as both a skip and its own 28 tests.
residual_risk: The 45 recovered tests are 45 tests nobody has watched fail. They pass today, but they have never guarded anything, so their real value is unproven until one of them catches something. Related and larger: 28 of the 45 were not skipped, they were never COLLECTED, because tests/test_sydney_water_gsp_ingest.py calls pytest.importorskip('shapely') at module level. The ratchet did not miss the file entirely -- it counted it as ONE skip, so 28 dark tests were logged with the weight of one, under-reported 28-fold by the guard built specifically to make dark tests visible -- and they were only found because doc_claims.py flagged shapely as declared in a file CI never installs. Counting skips is necessary and not sufficient; the collected-test total is the number that would have caught it, and no ratchet watches it. Logged in the baseline, not fixed here. Also unfixed by choice: DQ-54's three exposed scripts (cross_review.py, validate_schema_contract.py:408, qa_gate.py:1385) are swept and logged but untouched, on instruction to report only -- validate_schema_contract.py is the one worth doing first, because it uses git to locate the .env that supplies DATABASE_URL, so a wrong answer means the wrong credentials. And DQ-55's three stale documents are logged, not rewritten; one of them was already flagged as stale in June by another document and stayed stale, which is evidence that logging alone does not fix docs.

post_merge.db_reset: No. Nothing here reads or writes any database.
post_merge.secrets: No credentials are read, written or logged.
post_merge.manual_verify: Yes. Confirm the first CI run after merge reports 3970 passed / 2 skipped and that the dependency-skip step prints 0 against a baseline of 0. If either library fails to install on the runner, the ratchet will say so rather than reverting quietly.
